definition.en-US: The text you send to a model, including your instructions and the material it should work on.

analogy.en-US: Like the note you give a waiter that says what you want and how you want it cooked.

definition.en-US: A program trained on large amounts of text that reads the text you give it and writes an answer.

analogy.en-US: Like a well-read friend who answers from everything they have read, and who can still get one detail wrong.

definition.en-US: The smallest unit of text a model reads and counts, which may be a word, part of a word, a character or a byte.

analogy.en-US: Like a bead on a string, where the length you pay for depends on how many beads are on it.

definition.en-US: The amount of text, counted in tokens, that a model can look at in one request.

analogy.en-US: Like the desk you work at, which can hold only so many papers at once.

definition.en-US: An answer that sounds confident but is factually incorrect or does not match the text it was given.

analogy.en-US: Like a student who writes a confident essay from memory and gets a date wrong without noticing.

definition.en-US: A set of rules that lets one program send a request to another program and receive a reply.

analogy.en-US: Like an order form at a restaurant, where the kitchen acts only on requests written in the agreed form.

definition.en-US: A secret code that identifies your account to a service, so the service knows whose requests to accept and whom to bill.

analogy.en-US: Like a library card number, which proves who you are and should be kept private.

definition.en-US: A named setting that your terminal passes to the programs it starts, so they can read the value without it being written in their files.

analogy.en-US: Like a note on the fridge that everyone in the house can read, instead of writing the phone number inside every letter.

definition.en-US: A check that repeats earlier test inputs after a change, to confirm that answers you accepted before are still accepted.

analogy.en-US: Like checking that the other rooms still work after you repaint one room.

definition.en-US: A maximum amount that a service lets you spend in a period, after which the service refuses further requests until you raise the limit or the period resets.

analogy.en-US: Like a prepaid phone plan that stops calls once the credit is used up.

definition.en-US: A notification that a service sends when your tracked spending reaches an amount you chose, without stopping your requests.

analogy.en-US: Like the low-fuel warning light, which comes on before the tank is empty.

definition.en-US: A fixed list of test inputs, each with the answer you accept, which you run again after every change.

analogy.en-US: Like a spelling test that you give to the same class each week to see whether it is improving.

definition.en-US: Text that tries to make a model ignore its instructions and follow new instructions hidden in the content it reads.

analogy.en-US: Like a note slipped into a stack of papers that tells you to ignore your boss and do something else instead.
